contract_plain_english: For a real-valued random variable X on a probability space (Ω, Σ, P), the source calls E X the expectation or mean and identifies it with the Lebesgue integral of X. It defines variance by Var(X) = E[(X − E X)^2]. The book omits expectation brackets and says nonlinear functions bind first, so the squared centered quantity is formed before applying E. The passage does not say what integrability, square-integrability, finiteness, or extended-value conventions govern these expressions. [Source: PDF page 1 / printed page 5, Section 1.1 opening paragraph and display, footnotes 1–2; anchors: 'expectation (also called mean)', 'Lebesgue integral', 'Var(X) = E(X − E X)^2', and 'nonlinear functions bind before expectation'.]
